item.title: Incertitude en Suède sur l'issue des élections législatives
item.description: Les élections législatives en Suède dimanche ont donné lieu à un coude-à-coude entre la coalition de droite au pouvoir et l'opposition de centre-gauche, laquelle dispose selon des résultats partiels d'une légère avance qui lui permettrait de stopper le virage conservateur du pays, à la tradition libérale.
item.dc:creator: Anna Ringstrom, Simon Johnson
item.content:encoded: Les élections législatives en Suède dimanche ont donné lieu à un coude-à-coude entre la coalition de droite au pouvoir et l'opposition de centre-gauche, laquelle dispose selon des résultats partiels d'une légère avance qui lui permettrait de stopper le virage conservateur du pays, à la tradition libérale. D'après l'autorité électorale, après dépouillement des suffrages dans 6.195 des 6.312 districts électoraux, le bloc de centre-gauche, dirigé par la cheffe de file des sociaux-démocrates Magdalena Andersson, est donné victorieux de 176 sièges sur les 349 que compte le Parlement suédois ("Riksdag"). La coalition de droite du Premier ministre sortant Ulf Kristersson est créditée de 173 sièges, montrent les résultats partiels. Etant donné l'écart infime dans les suffrages, les résultats définitifs ne devraient pas être connus avant mercredi, une fois pris en compte les bulletins des électeurs vivant à l'étranger. Si l'issue du scrutin ne devrait pas déboucher sur un changement dans la position pro-Europe et pro-Ukraine de Stockholm, un nouveau mandat d'Ulf Kristersson permettrait à celui-ci de faire avancer son programme très strict de lutte contre l'immigration. Au cours de la campagne électorale, le dirigeant conservateur s'est affranchi d'un tabou en exprimant son intention d'offrir des ministères aux Démocrates de Suède, un parti d'extrême droite plongeant ses racines dans la mouvance néo-nazie, avec le but d'ancrer la coalition gouvernementale à droite. Les Démocrates de Suède ont jusqu'à présent soutenu le gouvernement de Kristersson sans y participer. Nombre d'électeurs de droite ont dit penser qu'une victoire de leur camp équivaudrait à une validation des mesures ayant selon eux contribué à réduire la criminalité et de la politique anti-immigration mise en oeuvre par le gouvernement sortant. Toutefois, certains Suédois ont fait part de leurs craintes, disant considérer que l'invitation formulée par Ulf Kristersson à l'extrême droite dépassait les limites. Donné perdant au début de la campagne électorale, le Premier ministre conservateur a repris espoir ces dernières semaines en gagnant du terrain dans les sondages face à Magdalena Andersson. Cette tendance s'est inscrite sur fond de nouvelle percée des partis anti-immigration en Europe, avec la victoire du parti allemand d'extrême droite Alternative pour l'Allemagne (AfD) lors d'élections régionales organisées la semaine dernière. Selon un sondage de sortie des urnes réalisé pour la chaîne de télévision publique SVT, le parti Démocrates de Suède, dont le chef de file est Jimmie Akesson, obtiendrait cependant environ 17% des voix seulement, soit un recul de trois points par rapport à 2022.

item.title: Zverev hails mother's unwavering belief after US Open triumph
item.description: Family was at the heart of Alexander Zverev's U.S. Open triumph on Sunday as the German saluted the members of his inner circle and paid a heartfelt tribute to his mother for refusing to let diabetes define his future.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Family was at the heart of Alexander Zverev's U.S. Open triumph on Sunday as the German saluted the members of his inner circle and paid a heartfelt tribute to his mother for refusing to let diabetes define his future. The top seed beat American Ben Shelton 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 at Flushing Meadows to finish a spectacular year at the Grand Slams in which he proved his doubters wrong by going from perennial nearly man to two-time major champion. Shortly after his victory, Zverev reserved special praise for his mother Irina, a former professional tennis player, and credited her with ensuring type 1 diabetes never limited his ambitions in life. "When your 4-year-old son is diagnosed with diabetes and doctors in the office tell you that life and sports will be very limited for that child, it takes a very strong mother to say 'my son will be whatever he wants to be'," Zverev said. "'If he wants to be a tennis player, he'll be a tennis player. If he wants to do something else, he'll do something else, but this illness will not define us'. "I'm happy that we worked through it and we're doing the things that we're doing now. My mother is the most important and strongest person I know because it takes an unbelievably strong woman to do what she did." The 29-year-old thanked his team, which includes his father Alexander Zverev Sr and his brother Mischa, for their hard work that had delivered him another Grand Slam trophy to add to his Olympic gold medal from the Tokyo Games five years ago. "We went almost 30 years without winning a Grand Slam title and now we've won two in a span of three months," Zverev said. "I think God has seen how hard we've worked, how much we've suffered, how much pain we went through and I think that 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before." SCARS OF 2020 Zverev had come agonisingly close to capturing his maiden Grand Slam title in New York in 2020, leading Dominic Thiem by two sets to none and later serving for the match in the fifth set before losing. He finally won his first major crown at this year's French Open after defeating Flavio Cobolli in five sets, and the German doubled his tally in New York despite making a shaky start to the fortnight. He also reached the Wimbledon final this year, falling to Jannik Sinner in four sets. "The scars of the 2020 (U.S. Open) final, they disappeared after I won in Paris. I said at Wimbledon, though I lost in the final, I enjoyed the match ... enjoyed playing on Centre Court in front of an amazing crowd," Zverev said. "Before winning in Paris, I felt a lot of stress all the time, because there was always a question mark. 'Will I ever win one?' Now it's more of a joy to play those kinds of finals." With Sinner sidelined by a knee injury and Carlos Alcaraz having just returned from a wrist problem, Zverev reluctantly accepted that he was the man to beat in men's tennis after a strong finish to the Grand Slam season. "Four or five months ago, when both of them were healthy, I wasn't. I was losing to Jannik all the time," he added. "So if everyone is healthy, Jannik is still ahead. It's as simple as that."

item.title: Anthropic tells investors it will be profitable for second straight quarter, FT reports
item.description: Anthropic has told shareholders that its adjusted operating income will be positive for a second straight quarter, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing multiple people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has told shareholders that its adjusted operating income will be positive for a second straight quarter, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing multiple people with knowledge of the matter. Anthropic's gross margins are above 80% before accounting for revenue shared with distribution partners, including Amazon (AMZN.O) , and the cost of training its model, the newspaper said. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside of regular business hours.

item.title: Attack hits Panguna camp as Bougainville backs copper mine restart
item.description: Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama condemned an attack on a mining camp at Panguna and said his government would press ahead with plans to reopen the long-shuttered copper mine despite opposition from some groups.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama condemned an attack on a mining camp at Panguna and said his government would press ahead with plans to reopen the long-shuttered copper mine despite opposition from some groups. The Panguna mine, once among the world's biggest open-pit copper operations, has been closed for nearly three decades following conflict that devastated the autonomous Papua New Guinea region. Plans are now underway to get the mine back up and running. Personnel were assaulted and equipment was destroyed at the mine camp in Panguna, Toroama's office said in a statement late Sunday. It did not give details on injuries, identify those involved or say how much equipment was damaged. Toroama said the Bougainville Police Service and community leaders were working to identify suspects and prevent further violence. Those responsible would face the law, he said. The potential reopening is politically and economically significant for Bougainville, which is seeking to strengthen its economy as it pursues a path [USN:L6N44N17U TEXT:"toward independence"] from Papua New Guinea. Supporters say renewed mining could create jobs, improve infrastructure and generate revenue for public services. But reopening the mine remains contentious because of its history and ongoing questions over landowner consent, environmental safeguards and how mining benefits would be shared. Toroama said the incident would not weaken the government's resolve to reopen Panguna.

item.title: China's Ligent seeks about $723 million in Hong Kong IPO, targets AI-related expansion
item.description: China's Ligent Technologies seeks to raise about HK$5.67 billion ($723 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering to fund product development and expand production, showed a prospectus filed at the stock exchange on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Jino, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: China's Ligent Technologies seeks to raise about HK$5.67 billion ($723 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering to fund product development and expand production, showed a prospectus filed at the stock exchange on Monday. The maker of fibre optic communications equipment has received $340 million from cornerstone investors, or 47% of the base share sale, the prospectus showed. Cornerstone investors are institutions that agree to buy shares before trading begins. Cornerstone investors include Primavera Investment Fund, GigaDevice, Amlogic Hong Kong, Mirae Asset Securities HK, PAG, ORIX-backed Turquoise Hime, Barings, GF Fund and E Fund, Ligent said in its prospectus. Ligent has offered 172 million shares at an offer price of HK$32.96 apiece, equivalent to a market value of HK$32.4 billion ($4.13 billion), the prospectus showed. The offer includes an option for underwriters to sell up to 25.8 million additional shares. The company, controlled by Chinese technology conglomerate Hisense Group Holdings, plans to list its shares in Hong Kong on September 22, the prospectus showed. Reuters [USN:L4N44V05L TEXT:"reported"] on September 3, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Ligent planned to launch the IPO as soon as September 14 with the aim of raising around $800 million, and that it could list in Hong Kong on September 22. Ligent makes optical transceivers, optical chips and network terminals used in data centres, cloud computing and telecommunications networks. It said it will use IPO proceeds to fund research and development, expand production capacity and support general corporate purposes. In the prospectus, Ligent disclosed a 29.7% net profit increase at 661 million yuan ($98.5 million) for the six months ended June 30 versus the same period a year earlier, and a 27.9% increase in revenue at 5.39 billion yuan. Sales of data-centre transceivers, Ligent's largest business, rose 36.6% to 3.74 billion yuan, driven by demand for equipment used in artificial intelligence and cloud computing, the prospectus showed. Hisense is set to retain 40.1% of Ligent after the IPO in the event that the overallotment option is not used, from 48.6% before the offering. Citigroup (C.N) and CITIC Securities (600030.SS) are joint sponsors of the deal. ($1 = 7.8425 Hong Kong dollars) ($1 = 6.7080 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Oil prices jump more than 2% after new strikes on Saudi, Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Brent crude futures rose to $108.23 per barrel.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Howe
item.content:encoded: Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Monday, after new Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks on ships in the Gulf compounded supply concerns following the closure of a key Saudi oil pipeline. Brent crude futures rose $2.90, or 2.77%, to $107.51 per barrel as of 2313 GMT. WTI futures rose $2.27, or 2.27%, to $102.32 per barrel. Prices had initially risen more than 3% at market open. Saudi Arabian state media on Sunday released video footage of damage to homes and a mosque from what it said was a [USN:L6N45500C TEXT:"Houthi attack"] on the country's southern Jazan province. The Houthis said they had also struck a Saudi military base in a neighbouring province. A vessel in the Strait of Hormuz was struck by a projectile, causing a fire and forcing the crew to be evacuated, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said on Sunday. Iran said one person was killed and four crew wounded aboard an Iranian commercial vessel struck off its coast. Oil prices had been expected to rise on Monday amid growing concerns about risks to supply from Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, whose East-West oil pipeline was shut on Friday by a [USN:L6N4530LJ TEXT:"drone strike"] that originated in Iraq. The loss of the pipeline, which helped Saudi Arabia re-route its exports avoiding the Strait of Hormuz, [USN:L6N455029 TEXT:"threatens"] up to 4% of global oil supply. Meanwhile, Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis had reached the strategic island of [USN:L6N4530LJ TEXT:"Perim"] on Friday, moving to tighten their control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another key oil transit lane that has been shipping 4-5% of global supply in recent months. Oil [USN:L1N45303L TEXT:"surged"] 8% higher on the week due to the disruptions, rising above $100 for the first time since July. "Looking ahead, unless this week's talks in Oman produce something operational — or the East-West pipeline is brought back online quickly — the risk is that crude oil continues to extend its gains toward the $119.48 high of early March," IG market analyst Tony Sycamore said in a note on Sunday. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said on X later on Sunday, however, that a scheduled Monday meeting in Oman between Gulf countries and Iran to discuss the Strait of Hormuz had been postponed. No peace talks have been held in the war, launched six months ago by the United States and Israel, since an interim agreement in June collapsed after a few weeks.

item.title: Tennis-Zverev bat Shelton pour s'offrir son premier sacre à l'US Open
item.description: L'Allemand Alexander Zverev, tête de série numéro une à l'US Open, a remporté dimanche le tournoi new-yorkais pour la première fois de sa carrière en battant en finale l'Américain Ben Shelton (6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Allemand Alexander Zverev, tête de série numéro une à l'US Open, a remporté dimanche le tournoi new-yorkais pour la première fois de sa carrière en battant en finale l'Américain Ben Shelton (6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2). Il s'agit du deuxième titre en Grand Chelem de sa carrière, après sa victoire à Roland-Garros plus tôt cette année.

item.title: トランプ氏、ＡＩ開発で米の主導権維持必要と強調 過度な懸念否定
item.description:
Bo Erickson Padraic Halpin
[ドンベッグ（アイルランド） １３日 ロイター] - トランプ米...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トランプ氏、ＡＩ開発で米の主導権維持必要と強調　過度な懸念否定 7:10 配信

写真はトランプ米大統領。9月12日、アイルランドのダブリンで撮影。REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

Bo Erickson　Padraic Halpin

[ドンベッグ（アイルランド）　１３日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１３日、訪問先のアイルランドで記者団に対し、人工知能（ＡＩ）に懐疑的な見方を示す人々について「起こりもしないことを持ち出す非常に否定的な勢力だ」と批判した。その上で「ＡＩ競争で勝つ者が勝者になる」と述べ、米国がＡＩ分野の主導権を維持する必要性を強調した。

トランプ氏は、ＡＩ産業は開発速度を落とすべきか、あるいは規制を強化すべきかとの質問に「米国はＡＩで中国をリードしている。世界で最も高度な国であり、その地位を維持したい」と語った。

さらに「ガードレールを設けることはできる。しかし起こらないようなことを持ち出す非常にネガティブな多くの人々がいると思う」と述べ、安全性を巡る過度な懸念を退けた。

米国では、ＡＩ開発企業アンソロピックの研究者２人が、急速に進歩するＡＩ技術が近い将来に人類絶滅を招く可能性があると警告したことを受け、ＡＩを巡る議論が活発化している。

こうした研究者による警告を受け、一部のＡＩ企業首脳はモデル開発の速度を抑えるべきだと主張。アンソロピックのダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１２日、開発ペースを管理し、リスクへの対応時間を確保するための「３段階の枠組み」を提案した。この提案には、スペースＸを率いるイーロン・マスク氏やオープンＡＩのサム・アルトマンＣＥＯら複数の業界幹部が賛同を表明した。

一方でアモデイ氏は１３日に放送された米ＣＢＳテレビの番組「フェイス・ザ・ネーション」で、米中ＡＩ企業間の競争は開発速度に「制限速度」を設けようとする上で「最も難しいジレンマだ」と指摘した。

同氏は「先行しようとする誘因や軍事的優位性が非常に大きいことを考えると、相手がルールを破っていないことを確認する仕組みは完全なものでなければならない。それには何年もの取り組みが必要で、正直なところ実現可能かどうか分からない」と語った。

アンソロピックを辞職後に警告を発した研究者のジェイコブ・コクソン氏は、米国が他国と協力して開発ペースを管理する必要があると訴えた。コクソン氏はＮＢＣテレビの番組「ミート・ザ・プレス」で「国際的な協調が必要だ。そうでなければ、中国との競争を続けることになり、それは同様に危険になり得る」と述べた。

item.title: トランプ氏、ＦＯＭＣ控え「米国は世界最低金利であるべき」
item.description:
Bo Erickson Padraic Halpin Conor Humphries
[ドゥーンベグ（アイルランド） ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トランプ氏、ＦＯＭＣ控え「米国は世界最低金利であるべき」 7:06 配信

写真はトランプ米大統領。9月13日、アイルランドのクレア州ドゥーンベッグで撮影。REUTERS/Cathal McNaughton

Bo Erickson　Padraic Halpin　Conor Humphries

[ドゥーンベグ（アイルランド） １３日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の次回政策会合を数日後に控えた１３日、米国は世界で最も金利が低い国であるべきだと述べた。

アイルランドで開催されたゴルフ大会で記者団に対し、ＦＲＢの政策決定者が今週の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）会合で利上げを行うかどうかは分からないと発言。しかし、インフレや経済に関するＦＲＢのデータがどうであれ、米国は「世界で最も低い金利を適用すべきだ」と主張した。

ＦＲＢは１５─１６日にＦＯＭＣの会合を開く。１１日に発表された８月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が４カ月ぶりの大幅上昇を記録したため、利上げ観測が強まっている。

共和党は米連邦議会の両院で僅差での過半数を維持できるかどうかが決まる中間選挙をわずか数週間後に控える。最近のロイター／イプソスの世論調査によると、利上げは生活費の高騰に対する有権者の懸念をさらに強める可能性がある。

インフレが継続する中、トランプ氏の支持率は低下している。同氏は、ＦＲＢの金利水準が米国を犠牲にして他国を助けていると主張してきた。

トランプ氏は１３日、「私は誰よりも数字に詳しい。世界最高の信用力を持つ米国が他国を豊かにしているのだ」と語った。

パウエル前ＦＲＢ議長を頻繁に批判してきたトランプ氏は、自身が指名したウォーシュ氏が今年初めに議長に就任して以来、ＦＲＢを支持する姿勢を示してきた。だが最近は、自身の要求をより明確に打ち出している。２週間前には「金利を下げろ。さもないと、米国が貿易赤字となっている国との取引を停止する」とソーシャルメディアに投稿した。

トランプ氏は１３日、米国へ戻る飛行機に乗る前に記者団に対し、「われわれは他国との貿易赤字を望んでいない。黒字あるいは少なくとも収支均衡を望んでいる」とあらためて述べた。

ハセット国家経済会議（ＮＥＣ）委員長はＦＯＸニュースに対し、ＦＲＢが金利をどう動かそうとも、トランプ氏は「何よりもウォーシュＦＲＢ議長の独立性を擁護するだろう」と語った。ただ同時にトランプ氏自身の意向も強調し、「もし利上げとなれば、大統領は決して大喜びはしないだろう」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ＦＯＭＣと日銀会合、金融政策ウイークの注目点＝植野大作氏 コラム：なお残る米9月利上げの公算、 ＦＯＭＣ議事要旨が示唆 アングル：米財務長官のレポ・ファシリティ上限引き上げ要求、リスクを伴う可能性 アングル：米国債「ツイスト・スティープ化」、ＦＲＢの信認巡る懸念反映か アングル：利上げに距離置くウォーシュＦＲＢ議長、7月ＦＯＭＣで試練に直面 最終更新: 9/14(月) 8:58 ロイター

item.title: US Open men's singles champion Alexander Zverev
item.description: Factbox on Alexander Zverev, who beat American eighth seed Ben Shelton 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 in the U.S. Open final on Sunday to win his second Grand Slam title:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Factbox on Alexander Zverev, who beat American eighth seed Ben Shelton 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 in the U.S. Open final on Sunday to win his second Grand Slam title: Age: 29 Nation: Germany ATP Ranking: 2 Seeding: 1 Grand Slam titles: 2 (French Open 2026, U.S. Open 2026) EARLY LIFE * Born in Hamburg and began playing tennis at the age of five. CAREER TO DATE * A former world number one junior, he began competing on the International Tennis Federation junior circuit at the age of 13. * Made his ATP Tour main-draw debut at the German Open in 2013 and won his first junior Grand Slam title at the Australian Open in 2014. * Won his first ATP title at the St Petersburg Open in 2016 after breaking into the top 30. * Claimed his first Masters title in Rome in 2017 and followed it up with victory at the Canadian Open, finishing the year ranked fourth in the world. * Beat world number one Novak Djokovic to win the ATP Finals in 2018. * Reached the Australian Open semi-finals in 2020 before advancing to his first Grand Slam final at the U.S. Open, where he lost to Dominic Thiem despite leading by two sets. * Won gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and reached the semi-finals of the French Open and U.S. Open before claiming a second ATP Finals title. * Was forced to retire from his 2022 French Open semi-final against Rafa Nadal after tearing ankle ligaments. He was sidelined for several months after undergoing surgery. * Returned in 2023 and reached the French Open semi-finals for a third consecutive year. * Advanced to his second Grand Slam final at the 2024 French Open but lost to Carlos Alcaraz in five sets. * Reached the final of the 2025 Australian Open, where he was beaten by defending champion Jannik Sinner in straight sets. * Made the semi-finals of the 2026 Australian Open before losing to Alcaraz in five sets. * Beat Flavio Cobolli in five sets in the French Open final to win his first Grand Slam title and become Germany's first men's major champion since Boris Becker won the 1996 Australian Open. * Arrived at the 2026 U.S. Open as the top seed following the withdrawal of world number one Jannik Sinner due to a persistent knee injury. After a shaky start that featured five-set matches in each of the opening two rounds, Zverev found his rhythm and went on to claim his second Grand Slam title.

item.title: Zverev derrota a Shelton y se lleva el título del Abierto de EEUU
item.description: El cabeza de serie número uno, Alexander Zverev, dejó atrás sus amargos recuerdos del Abierto de Estados Unidos al imponerse al estadounidense Ben Shelton por 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7 y 6-2 en la final del domingo, alzándose con el título seis años después de que dejó escapar una oportunidad de oro.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: El cabeza de serie número uno, Alexander Zverev, dejó atrás sus amargos recuerdos del Abierto de Estados Unidos al imponerse al estadounidense Ben Shelton por 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7 y 6-2 en la final del domingo, alzándose con el título seis años después de que dejó escapar una oportunidad de oro. El tenista alemán desperdició una ventaja de dos sets en la final de 2020 contra el austriaco Dominic Thiem, pero ahora, armado con la mentalidad de un campeón tras su triunfante victoria en Roland Garros en junio, rompió los corazones de los estadounidenses con una actuación arrolladora frente a Shelton. La afición local deseaba ver a Shelton poner fin a una sequía de 23 años sin un ganador local en la competencia individual masculina del Grand Slam estadounidense, pero el octavo cabeza de serie nunca encontró su mejor forma en su primera final de un torneo de Grand Slam. En un duelo entre dos de los jugadores más explosivos del tenis, Zverev tuvo toda la potencia inicial, mientras que la falta de experiencia de Shelton quedó patente con una doble falta en un punto de break en el primer juego. Shelton protagonizó uno de los mejores puntos del partido en el sexto juego, lanzándose a por un golpe cortado e imponiéndose en un tenso intercambio en la red. Animado por su equipo, el estadounidense incorporó tácticas de saque y volea en un intento por cambiar el rumbo del partido, pero la estrategia resultó ineficaz y le entregó el set a Zverev con una doble falta. El público local intentó poner nervioso a Zverev en el segundo set, vitoreando con entusiasmo tras una doble falta que cometió en el noveno juego. Pero el alemán se mantuvo concentrado y se puso con una ventaja de 5-0 en el tie-break mientras los aficionados coreaban desesperadamente "¡Vamos, Ben!". En un momento pareció que Zverev se llevaría el partido en tres sets corridos, ya que salvó un punto de break en el sexto juego con un letal golpe ganador de revés. La frustración de Shelton llegó a su punto álgido dos juegos más tarde, cuando resbaló y cayó al suelo, lo que provocó que el estadounidense soltara una palabrota. Pero Shelton se mantuvo firme y dominó a su rival con una serie de potentes golpes desde la línea de fondo para romperle el servicio y forzar un cuarto set. La resistencia de Shelton solo retrasó lo inevitable, ya que Zverev superó un intercambio de 25 golpes para asegurarse un break temprano en el set decisivo. No soltó esa ventaja en ningún momento y, finalmente, tuvo la oportunidad de levantar el trofeo del Abierto de Estados Unidos en su undécima participación en este Grand Slam sobre pista dura.

item.title: Zverev banishes US Open demons with victory over Shelton
item.description: The German added the New York title to his collection after winning the French Open trophy earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Top seed Alexander Zverev banished bitter U.S. Open memories to beat American Ben Shelton 6-3 7-6(2) 5-7 6-2 in the final on Sunday, capturing the title six years after letting a golden opportunity slip through his fingers. The German squandered a two-set lead in the 2020 title match against Austrian Dominic Thiem but now armed with a champion's mentality following his breakthrough triumph at Roland Garros in June, he broke American hearts with a devastating display against Shelton. "I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before," Zverev said during the presentation ceremony. The home fans were desperate to see Shelton end a 23-year American men's Grand Slam drought but the eighth seed never found his top form in his first major final. "I know that today 99.9% of the people wanted Ben to win so I'm very sorry," said Zverev. "Even though I know that the crowd was against me, the crowd was always incredibly fair and we as players we appreciate it." Zverev was so focused on the job at hand, he did not even realise he had won the title when Shelton smacked a service return long. As the umpire announced 'Game, set and match Zverev', the German headed back to the baseline, ready to receive Shelton's serve. It took him a few seconds to register why the cheering fans were giving him a standing ovation -- as he belatedly cracked a smile and ran to the net to embrace Shelton. He was beaming again as he was handed a Grand Slam record $5.5 million winner's prize. ZVEREV GETS HOT START In a battle between two of tennis' most explosive players, it was Zverev who had all the early firepower, as Shelton's inexperience showed with a double fault on break point in the opening game. Shelton produced one of the points of the match in the sixth game, scrambling to reach a drop shot and prevailing in a tense exchange at the net. Encouraged by his team, the American mixed in serve-and-volley tactics in an attempt to shift the momentum, but the move proved ineffective and he handed Zverev the set with a double fault. The partisan crowd tried to get under Zverev's skin in the second set, cheering wildly after he produced a double fault in the ninth game. But the German refused to get distracted, surging to a 5-0 lead in the tiebreak as the fans desperately chanted "Let's go, Ben!" Zverev looked like he would roll to the finish line in the third set as he saved a break point in the sixth game with a lethal backhand winner. Shelton's frustration boiled over two games later when he slipped and crashed to the court, prompting the American to let out an expletive. But Shelton dug in his heels, subduing his opponent with a series of powerful groundstrokes from the baseline to break serve and force a fourth set. Shelton's resilience only delayed the inevitable as Zverev came through a 25-shot rally to secure an early break in the deciding set. He never let go of that advantage as he finally got the chance to hoist the U.S. Open trophy on his 11th appearance at the hardcourt major. "My successes are a gift, the failures are a gift, and being here playing in front of you guys is a gift," said Shelton, the first Black American man in 54 years to contest the New York final after Arthur Ashe. His girlfriend, Olympic champion soccer player [USN:L4N455006 TEXT:"Trinity Rodman"] , made it to his player's box after racing 200 miles from her Washington Spirit game, which largely overlapped with the start of his match. 'JANNIK IS STILL AHEAD' The victory will no doubt help Zverev move beyond a series of Grand Slam disappointments. The German's career has also been overshadowed by allegations of [USN:L6N42F07A TEXT:"domestic violence"], which he has repeatedly denied. His two majors this season have made a dent in the duopoly of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, who won all eight Grand Slam titles across 2024 and 2025. Alcaraz, who won this year's Australian Open, exited the U.S. Open in a quarter-final defeat by Shelton after a long injury layoff while Sinner pulled out injured before the tournament began after winning Wimbledon. Asked if he considered himself the world's top player now, Zverev said, "With Jannik Sinner being injured and Carlos Alcaraz coming back from injury after four months, right now this moment, probably yes. "Both of them healthy and both of them at the top of their game, maybe not. "If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead. It's as simple as that."

item.title: 投機筋が円買い越し転換、2月末以来 円キャリー巻き戻し終了の見方
item.description:
Atsuko Aoyama
[東京 １４日 ロイター] - 投機筋が前週、２月末以来で初めて円の買い越しに転換したこと...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
投機筋が円買い越し転換、2月末以来　円キャリー巻き戻し終了の見方 6:55 配信

日本円と米ドルの紙幣。2023年3月10日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 １４日 ロイター] - 投機筋が前週、２月末以来で初めて円の買い越しに転換したことが最新のデータ（８日時点）で分かった。市場では円のポジションが中立化され、円キャリーの巻き戻しがいったん終了したとの見方が聞かれる。８日にはドルが１５２円台まで下落し、１６０円超で推移していた月初から７円以上円高が進行していた。

米商品先物取引委員会（ＣＦＴＣ）が１４日までに公表した建玉報告によると、投機筋のポジション動向を映すとされるＩＭＭ通貨先物非商業部門の８日時点の取り組み状況で、円の買い越しは１万０７９６枚と、９万２２２７枚の売り越しだった前の週から買い越しに転換した。買い越しに転じたのは２月２４日時点のデータ以来初めて。

市場では「円キャリーの巻き戻しがいったん終了し、ポジションが中立化された。ドルが１５２円を下回る可能性がかなり減った」（あおぞら銀行の諸我晃チーフ・マーケット・ストラテジスト）との声が聞かれた。市場では前週の円高進行の背景として、日銀の利上げペース加速に関する思惑や日米当局による円安是正の意向が指摘されている。

データの内訳をみると、円の売り建玉は１６万７９９５枚と、前の週の２０万９３９６枚から２割弱減少。一方、円の買い建玉は１７万８７９１枚で、１１万７１６９枚から５割以上増加、２０２５年１２月初旬以来の多さとなった。

円売りと円買いの双方の建玉が残存していることを巡り、「双方に巻き戻しのリスクがある」（ＳＭＢＣ日興証券の丸山凜途シニア金利・為替ストラテジスト）との声も聞かれる。円売りの建玉は３月末の水準に減っているものの、２０２４年７月の介入後に約１５円の円高が生じた２０２４年８月中旬の６万３９９７枚を１０万枚以上上回っている。

item.title: North Korea says missile launches were part of live-fire drills
item.description: North Korea said on Monday that its launch of several missiles on Saturday was part of a live-fire drill involving long-range artillery and missile units, according to state media KCNA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea said on Monday that its launch of several missiles on Saturday was part of a live-fire drill involving long-range artillery and missile units, according to state media KCNA. The "joint firepower attack drill" involved five army units and tested several weapon systems, including attack drones, tactical cruise missiles, tactical ballistic missiles, and large-calibre multiple rocket launchers, KCNA said. The drill would boost the morale of the troops and improve their capabilities to "completely collapse the enemy" whenever ordered, KCNA said, citing an artillery director. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff [USN:L1N4530VM TEXT:"said"] on Saturday that North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles, which flew about 250 km (155 miles) toward the sea off its east coast. The launch came a day after South Korea, the United States and Japan wrapped up the five-day trilateral Freedom Edge exercise focused on countering North Korean threats. KCNA's report came two days after the launch, believed to be the 13th known ballistic missile launch event this year. North Korean state media had remained silent on several previous recent missile tests reported by South Korea. "This was not a test of a single weapon system but a demonstration of an integrated strike network," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies in Seoul. North Korea appeared to be showcasing its ability to coordinate drones, cruise missiles, ballistic missiles and rocket artillery through a unified command-and-control system, Lim said. The absence of leader Kim Jong Un and the delayed report suggested Pyongyang sought to present the event as a "technical and practical military exercise" while calibrating tensions, Lim said. "North Korea is also collecting operational data for actual deployment and demonstrating tactics aimed at saturating South Korean and U.S. missile defences through simultaneous attacks by weapons with different flight characteristics."

item.title: Brandon Lowe's pinch-hit heroics help Pirates evade sweep by Cubs
item.description: Brandon Lowe drove in two runs with a pinch-hit single in the sixth inning as the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Chicago Cubs 4-3 Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Lowe drove in two runs with a pinch-hit single in the sixth inning as the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Chicago Cubs 4-3 Sunday. The Cubs (83-67) fell into a tie with the Phillies for the first National League wild-card spot. Philadelphia beat Atlanta 9-4 Sunday. Chicago hosts the Braves in a three-game series starting Monday. The Pirates (75-75) avoided the sweep with the win. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (8-5) gave up seven hits and four runs in 5 1/3 innings. The southpaw walked two and struck out three in 88 pitches. Pirates starter Bubba Chandler (8-9) gave up five hits and three runs in 5 1/3 innings. The right-hander walked four and struck out three in 90 pitches. Mason Montgomery picked up his 13th save with a scoreless ninth inning. The Pirates started the scoring in the first when Konnor Griffin led off with a single and Oneil Cruz walked. Bryan Reynolds singled in Griffin for a 1-0 lead. Chandler only allowed one Cub to reach second base through 4 2/3 innings before Chicago broke through. Pedro Ramirez started the rally with a two-out walk, setting up Miguel Amaya for a two-run home run to left to put the Cubs in front 2-1. The Pirates fought back in the sixth when Reynolds walked to lead off and Rafael Flores Jr. singled. Nick Gonzales followed with a long drive to right over the head of Seiya Suzuki. The ball was lost in the ivy for a ground-rule double that tied the game 2-2. Boyd struck out Ryan O'Hearn for the first out of the inning, and Aaron Civale replaced him to face Jake Mangum. Mangum walked and Lowe followed with his single to center, scoring Flores and Gonzales to make it 4-2 Pirates. The Cubs cut the deficit to one run in the sixth, when Michael Busch singled with one out and Alex Bregman doubled to left. Ian Happ walked to load the bases and Busch scored when Nico Hoerner grounded out. --Field Level Media

item.title: Guardians creep closer to AL Central lead by hammering Twins
item.description: Steven Kwan, Jo Adell and Travis Bazzana hit home runs in the Cleveland Guardians' 9-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Sunday in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Steven Kwan, Jo Adell and Travis Bazzana hit home runs in the Cleveland Guardians' 9-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Sunday in Minneapolis. Kwan was 3-for-4 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and two runs while Bazzana added a walk, three RBIs and two runs and Adell scored two and drove in two for the Guardians (76-74), who moved within a half-game of the American League Central-leading Chicago White Sox. Trevor Larnach homered and doubled and Luke Keaschall added two hits for the Twins (70-79), who have lost three of their last four. Tanner Bibee (6-15) got the win by giving up two runs and four hits in 6 2/3 innings with two walks and seven strikeouts. Minnesota starter Joe Ryan (6-10) allowed four runs on seven hits in four innings with a walk and a strikeout. Kwan put the Guardians on top with a leadoff home run. He hit Ryan's 1-0 four-seam fastball into the overhang above the right field wall for his third homer of the year. Adell's home run leading off the third made it 2-0. He blasted Ryan's 0-1 four-seam fastball an estimated 451 feet into the third deck in left field. The exit velocity was 116.8 mph on Adell's 21st homer. Kody Clemens' two-out, run-scoring double in the bottom of the third put the Twins on the board for a 2-1 game. The Guardians responded with two in the fourth on Kwan's RBI double and Bazzana's two-out, run-producing single to stretch their lead to 4-1. Bazzana's two-run homer off Travis Adams made it 6-1 in the sixth. His 12th home run sailed into the right-center-field stands. Larnarch's 13th home run leading off the seventh pulled the Twins within 6-2. But Cleveland added three in the ninth on Adell's RBI double, a sacrifice fly by Nathaniel Lowe and a run-scoring double from Angel Martinez. Minnesota first baseman Royce Lewis left the game in the fifth with left shoulder soreness. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eugenio Suarez's homer, late plays lift Reds past Brewers
item.description: Elly De La Cruz scored the go-ahead run on Tyler Stephenson's sacrifice fly in the eighth inning, lifting the visiting Cincinnati Reds to a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Elly De La Cruz scored the go-ahead run on Tyler Stephenson's sacrifice fly in the eighth inning, lifting the visiting Cincinnati Reds to a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday afternoon. Cincinnati's Eugenio Suarez launched a three-run homer in the sixth inning, marking his second homer in as many games. De La Cruz singled off Abner Uribe (5-3) to lead off the eighth inning and advanced to third on rookie Sal Stewart's base hit. Stephenson stepped up two batters later and lofted a sacrifice fly to right field to plate De La Cruz to give the Reds a 4-3 lead. De La Cruz and Stewart each had two of the Reds' eight hits to help the Reds (70-79) salvage the finale of a 1-5 road trip. Brandon Williamson (4-4) allowed one run on two hits in four innings in relief of Chase Burns. Brock Burke bridged the gap to Emilio Pagan, who worked the ninth inning to secure his 23rd save of the season. Joey Ortiz belted a two-run homer in the second inning and Jake Bauers went deep to lead off the seventh for the Brewers (93-57), who saw their five-game winning streak come to a halt. Milwaukee starter Robert Gasser allowed his third hit on a leadoff single to De La Cruz in the sixth inning. Antonio Senzatela relieved Gasser and permitted a single to Stewart before seeing Suarez deposit a 0-1 sinker over the wall in right-center field to stake Cincinnati to a 3-2 lead. Suarez's homer was his 24th of the season. Bauers sent a 1-0 fastball from Williamson over the wall in right-center field to forge a 3-3 tie. Bauers' homer was his 26th of the season and third in his last six games. Christian Yelich worked a one-out walk in the second inning before Ortiz deposited a 2-1 fastball from Burns over the wall in center field to open the scoring. The homer was Ortiz's ninth of the season. Uribe permitted one run on two hits in one inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: Agustin Ramirez blasts walk-off HR as Marlins take series from Dodgers
item.description: Pinch hitter Agustin Ramirez hit a two-run, walk-off homer in the ninth to give the Miami Marlins a 6-4 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Agustin Ramirez hit a two-run, walk-off homer in the ninth to give the Miami Marlins a 6-4 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday. Miami entered the eighth inning trailing 3-0 but pulled within one on a two-run single from Otto Lopez. The Marlins entered the ninth behind 4-2 with ex-Marlins pitcher Tanner Scott on the mound trying to close it out. Xavier Edwards' infield single, Jakob Marsee's bunt hit and Javier Sanoja's softly hit two-run double down the left field line tied the score 4-4 with nobody out. Los Angeles brought in Brock Stewart to gain the platoon advantage against Ramirez, who got a 94 mph fastball down the middle and belted it 407 feet to left center. Miami (74-76) won for just the third time in 10 contests, but the hosts won the three-game series as Los Angeles (90-59) dropped its second straight game after winning eight in a row. The loss ruined a great performance by Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula, who slugged a three-run homer for his first MLB hit and doubled off the wall. The 21-year-old outfielder, who made his MLB debut on Friday, finished the game 2-for-2 with a walk. The Marlins played a video tribute after the first inning for Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas, who plans to retire after this season. Rojas, 37, played for the Marlins from 2015-22. Rojas went 1-for-3 on Sunday, but he banged his right shoulder in the eighth when he made a diving attempt at Joe Mack's ground-ball single. After a brief delay, Rojas remained in the game before leaving for a pinch hitter in the ninth. Dodgers starter Emmet Sheehan allowed two hits and one walk over six scoreless innings. He struck out five and was in line for the win before his bullpen caved. Los Angeles took a 3-0 lead in the fourth as Will Smith doubled, Kyle Tucker walked and De Paula unloaded on a 98-mph Eury Perez fastball that he pulled 416 feet to right. Miami scored twice in the eighth against reliever Edgardo Henriquez as Mack and Esteury Ruiz singled and Heriberto Hernandez walked to load the bases. With two outs, Lopez singled off a 100.4-mph fastball to cut the deficit to 3-2. Scott came in and struck out Griffin Conine on three pitches, including two swings on pitches well out of the strike zone. Los Angeles extended its lead to 4-2 in the ninth as Alex Freeland singled, stole second and scored on Mookie Betts' double. --Field Level Media

item.title: Caleb Williams, Bears put up 59 on Panthers in record-setting opener
item.description: Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more and the Chicago Bears pulled away for a 59-37 victory against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Caleb Williams threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more and the Chicago Bears pulled away for a 59-37 victory against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte in the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. In the teams' season opener, D'Andre Swift scored three touchdown runs and rushed for 124 yards on 18 carries for Chicago. Williams completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and added 65 rushing yards. Kyle Monangai gained 100 yards on 10 carries, including a 61-yard TD. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw two of his three touchdown passes to Jalen Coker. Young was 23 of 37 for 361 yards with one interception. Coker made eight catches for 138 yards. Chuba Hubbard scored touchdowns on a run and a reception. The Panthers pulled even at 31-31 on Hubbard's 2-yard run with 9:02 left in the third quarter. From there, the Bears posted the next three touchdowns on runs by Swift (1 yard) and Monangai and Williams' 1-yard pass to Jahdae Walker. Later, Swift found the end zone from 28 yards out. Cairo Santos' 40-yard field goal for the Bears and Ryan Fitzgerald's 44-yarder for the Panthers left the teams tied at 24-24 late in the first half. Williams rambled 29 yards with 22 seconds left for a 31-24 lead. Chicago had 315 yards of first-half total offense. The points parade began early. After the Bears fumbled two snaps into the game, the Panthers went 42 yards for a touchdown on their first possession. Young threw 4 yards to Hubbard for the score. Chicago pulled even when Williams scrambled around the left side for a 9-yard touchdown to complete a nine-play drive. Swift ran 1 yard for a score later in the first quarter for the Bears' first lead. He had 65 first-quarter rushing yards. Chicago took over at the Carolina 41 following a Panthers punt and penalty. Cole Kmet's 22-yard reception produced the touchdown. Three plays later, the Panthers were in the end zone on Young's 51-yard pass to Coker. The Bears gambled on a fourth-down play at their own 21, failing to pick up 1 yard as Carolina took over and converted when Young raced 7 yards for a touchdown. The score was 21-21 just over 21 minutes into the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lions roar on offense before edging Saints 31-30 in OT
item.description: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 156 yards and two touchdowns, Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes to Amon-Ra St. Brown and the host Detroit Lions held off the New Orleans Saints 31-30 in overtime Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed for 156 yards and two touchdowns, Jared Goff threw two touchdown passes to Amon-Ra St. Brown and the host Detroit Lions held off the New Orleans Saints 31-30 in overtime Sunday afternoon. Goff passed for 206 yards and the Lions had to stop a two-point conversion on the final play to prevail. Detroit got the ball first in overtime and Goff threw a 4-yard TD pass to St. Brown for a 31-24 lead with 5:04 remaining. Tyler Shough drove the Saints down the field on the ensuing drive and threw an 8-yard touchdown pass to Noah Fant, but his two-point conversion pass was incomplete in the back of the end zone. Shough recovered from three turnovers to pass for 410 yards and three touchdowns, including a 9-yard strike to Juwan Johnson late in regulation that forced OT. Chris Olave hauled in 10 receptions for 182 yards. On the first play of the third quarter, Derrick Barnes intercepted Shough, giving the Lions the ball at the Saints' 41. Seven plays later, Gibbs ran 1 yard for his second touchdown and a 14-0 lead. On New Orleans' next possession, Shough fumbled while being sacked by Roger McCreary and DJ Wonnum recovered at the Saints' 25. Three plays later, Goff threw a 19-yard touchdown pass to St. Brown for a 21-0 lead. On the first play of the ensuing possession, Shough connected with Olave on a 47-yard completion, which soon led to Kendre Miller's 8-yard touchdown run. New Orleans forced a three-and-out and Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele trimmed the lead to 21-14 at the end of the third quarter. The Saints scored for a third straight possession when Daniel Carlson's 28-yard field goal pulled them within four points midway through the fourth quarter. Jake Bates' 23-yard field goal pushed the lead to 24-17 with 2:32 left. Shough helped New Orleans drive 75 yards in eight plays and just 1:25 of game time, ending with his TD pass to Johnson to tie the score with 1:07 left. Goff directed a 13-play, 89-yard drive in the first quarter that ended with Gibbs' 1-yard touchdown run. The 7-0 lead held up through the end of the first half. --Field Level Media

item.title: Phillies use seven-run eighth inning to stymie Braves
item.description: Alec Bohm's two-run double in the eighth inning sparked a seven-run rally and helped the visiting Philadelphia Phillies defeat the Atlanta Braves 9-4 on Sunday and salvage a contest from their three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alec Bohm's two-run double in the eighth inning sparked a seven-run rally and helped the visiting Philadelphia Phillies defeat the Atlanta Braves 9-4 on Sunday and salvage a contest from their three-game series. Philadelphia (83-67) cut Atlanta's lead in the National League East to five games with the victory. Atlanta's magic number to win the division remains seven. The Braves (88-62) won the season series 9-4. Facing reliever Dylan Lee (6-1) with the score tied 2-2, the Phillies had runners at second and third when Bohm drove a two-out liner to center field to score Bryce Harper and Trea Turner. Bryson Stott and J.T. Realmuto followed with run-scoring singles that stretched the lead to 6-2. Kyle Schwarber added a two-run single and Turner singled home a run. Realmuto and Stott each had three of the team's 16 hits and were among six players with multiple hits. Neither starter figured in the decision. Philadelphia's Andrew Painter pitched five strong innings and allowed one run on six hits and four walks, striking out three. Atlanta's Grant Holmes was only able to pitch four innings, allowing two runs on five hits and two walks. The Braves scored a run in the first. Michael Harris II led off with a single, advanced to third on Matt Olson's single and scored on Drake Baldwin's sacrifice fly. It was Baldwin's fourth RBI of the series. But Philadelphia scored twice in the second inning to take the lead. Realmuto hit a two-run homer, his 11th, that carried 405 feet into the left field seats. Atlanta first baseman Olson saved a run with his glove in the fifth inning. With runners on the corners, Schwarber grounded sharply to Olson, who stepped on the bag, checked the runner at third and threw out Justin Crawford at second base. The Braves tied the game in the seventh against reliever Jose Alvarado (4-3), the winning pitcher. Harris singled, took second on a wild pitch and scored on Olson's one-out single. It ended an eight-game scoreless streak for Alvarado. Olson, who went 3-for-5, added a two-run homer in the ninth inning, his 39th. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jonathan Aranda keys offensive outburst as Rays rout Astros
item.description: Jonathan Aranda homered twice with three RBIs, starter Freddy Peralta twirled five no-hit innings, and the Tampa Bay Rays completed their majors-best 15th series sweep Sunday by pummeling the Houston Astros 14-4 in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jonathan Aranda homered twice with three RBIs, starter Freddy Peralta twirled five no-hit innings, and the Tampa Bay Rays completed their majors-best 15th series sweep Sunday by pummeling the Houston Astros 14-4 in St. Petersburg, Fla. Falling a homer shy of the cycle, Victor Mesa Jr. was 3-for-5 with three runs and two RBIs. Richie Palacios was 2-for-4 with a three-run homer and scored twice, while Nick Fortes went deep for American League East-leading Tampa Bay (90-59). The Rays posted 15 hits and were 4-for-9 with runners in scoring position. Winning his fourth straight start, Peralta (9-11) fanned four and walked three in his five innings. The right-hander left with the Rays up 11-0. Isaac Paredes, Nick Allen and Nelson Velazquez homered for the Astros (75-75), who had only four hits and are 2-6 in the past eight games. In a season-shortest start of three innings, Hayden Wesneski (5-2) surrendered seven runs on six hits, but four markers were unearned. The right-hander struck out two and walked two. Batting cleanup in the first inning, Mesa extended his hitting streak to nine games with a triple to right to score Yandy Diaz and Junior Caminero, who had singled and doubled, respectively. Chandler Simpson's groundout made it 3-0. Peralta walked the bases loaded in the third, and Paredes hit a hard grounder that was fielded by Caminero. The third baseman took a couple of steps into foul territory and bounced a throw that first baseman Aranda awkwardly secured for the final out. The Rays made it 7-0 with four unearned runs in the third after a crucial two-out error by Houston shortstop Jeremy Pena, who dropped an easy, shallow popup as he jogged out to left field to score Mesa. Palacios followed with a high three-run homer to right for his 10th long ball and the touchdown lead. Aranda made it 8-0 in the fourth with an opposite-field solo shot, and Simpson's RBI single scored Mesa for his third run. In the fifth, Fortes drilled a two-run shot, his fifth, as the home side pulled ahead 11-0. Paredes spoiled the Rays' combined no-hit bid with a one-out homer to left, his 21st, in the sixth off reliever Brody Hopkins. Diaz (2-for-5, two runs, RBI) singled in Palacios in the seventh before Aranda hit homer No. 21. Allen and Velazquez rounded out the scoring by stroking homers in the eighth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nationals rally late to sweep Angels
item.description: Jacob Young doubled in the go-ahead run during a four-run eighth as the host Washington Nationals rallied to complete a three-game sweep of the Los Angeles Angels with a 6-5 victory on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jacob Young doubled in the go-ahead run during a four-run eighth as the host Washington Nationals rallied to complete a three-game sweep of the Los Angeles Angels with a 6-5 victory on Sunday afternoon. Daylen Lile, CJ Abrams, Yohandy Morales and James Wood provided two hits apiece for Washington (70-81) as Erik Tolman (1-1) collected his first major league win in relief. Jack Sinclair handled the ninth for his first big-league save. Moises Ballesteros and Zach Neto homered and Mike Trout doubled and walked twice for Los Angeles (56-93), which finished 3-6 on its nine-game, 11-day trip. Luke Murphy (0-3) allowed four runs on four hits in his inning of relief. Los Angeles took a 1-0 lead in the fourth inning when Ballesteros smashed his ninth home run, a 407-foot drive to center. The Angels extended the lead to 2-0 in the fifth when Neto hit his 26th home run, a 440-foot drive into the bleachers in center. Washington parlayed three hits and a hit batter into two runs in the sixth to forge a 2-2 tie. Abrams started the rally by hustling for a double and scoring on a Morales single to center. Lile followed with a single and Keibert Ruiz was hit by a pitch to load the bases. Morales scored the tying run on a fielder's choice by pinch hitter Brady House. Los Angeles scored two runs without a hit to take a 4-2 lead in the eighth. Neto and Wade Meckler walked and it appeared Tolman would get out of the jam when Vaughn Grissom hit a double-play grounder to short, but Abrams mishandled the ball for an error to load the bases. Neto scored on a wild pitch and Ballesteros followed with a sacrifice fly. Washington answered with four runs in the bottom half of the inning highlighted by an RBI triple by Lile off the wall in right center, a pinch-hit RBI single by Jorbit Vivas to tie it 4-4, and Young's double into the gap in left center. Dylan Crews scored Young on a single for a crucial insurance run. The Angels pulled within a run in the ninth when Josh Lowe led off with a double and scored on a groundout by Christian Moore. Sinclair struck out Neto to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Blue Jays power past Orioles, move to .500
item.description: The Toronto Blue Jays hit back-to-back-to-back home runs in the fifth inning Sunday and went on to defeat the visiting Baltimore Orioles 8-1.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Toronto Blue Jays hit back-to-back-to-back home runs in the fifth inning Sunday and went on to defeat the visiting Baltimore Orioles 8-1. George Springer, Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Kazuma Okamoto homered in succession against Trevor Rogers (10-10) in the rubber match of a three-game series between teams chasing a playoff berth in the American League. Guerrero was 4-for-5 with a double and two singles to go with his home run, which was only his ninth of the season and first at home. Springer also had a double and four RBIs. Toronto (75-75) leads the season series 6-4. That is the first tiebreaker for a playoff berth. Baltimore (72-78) went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 13 runners. Toronto starter Dylan Cease (11-5) struck out three batters in a row in the first inning after the Orioles loaded the bases on two walks and a single. Toronto took a 1-0 lead in the second. Charles McAdoo led off with a single to left and scored on a one-out double by Andres Gimenez on a flare that tipped off the glove of third baseman Christian Encarnacion-Strand. The Orioles tied the game in the fifth. Dylan Beavers led off with a double into the right-field corner and scored on Pete Alonso's bloop single down the right-field line. It was Alonso's 100th RBI of the season. Cease allowed one run, four hits and five walks and struck out nine in five innings. Toronto regained the lead in the bottom of the fifth when Springer clubbed a two-out homer to right on a 1-0 changeup. Guerrero followed by belting a 3-2 sweeper to left, which brought a huge reaction from the crowd. Okamoto was next to homer when lofted a 3-2 fastball to left. It was his 32nd homer and a Blue Jays rookie-record 85th RBI. Toronto's Braydon Fisher replaced Ricky Tiedemann with runners at the corners and two out in the sixth and retired Alonso on a called third strike. Rogers completed six innings, allowing four runs, seven hits and one walk with five strikeouts. Baltimore's Yaramil Hiraldo walked Brett Bateman with the bases loaded in the eighth to extend Toronto's lead. Cam Sanders took over and Beavers misplayed Springer's drive to left into a three-run double. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ravens ride Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers to 41-23 win at Indy
item.description: Derrick Henry scored three touchdowns and powered the Baltimore Ravens past the Colts 41-23 in Indianapolis on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Derrick Henry scored three touchdowns and powered the Baltimore Ravens past the Colts 41-23 in Indianapolis on Sunday. Henry had 144 rushing yards and buoyed Baltimore's offense in the second half after injuries knocked wide receivers Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane out. Flowers (hamstring) had five receptions for a career-high 150 yards before he was ruled out. Lane (wrist), who had one catch and a TD overturned by an offensive penalty, left in the third quarter. Baltimore's offense ran in overdrive early and the Ravens outgained the Colts 506-251. Lamar Jackson had 324 yards passing with a touchdown pass to Flowers and ran for a score. Colts running back Jonathan Taylor had 121 yards from scrimmage and ran for 98 yards on 19 carries with two touchdowns. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (19 of 31, 166 yards, one TD) was under pressure until his final snap. The Ravens had an interception, two sacks and 10 QB hits. Jones rushed the Colts down the field and found Tyler Warren for a 9-yard TD with 10 minutes to play, but the Ravens came back with Tyler Loop's 45-yard field goal for a 41-23 advantage with 4:09 to go. Ravens coach Jesse Minter won in his debut as a head coach while the Colts fell to 1-8-1 in regular-season openers the past 10 years. Without Flowers and Lane, the Ravens lulled the Colts to sleep with a heavy dose of Henry in the third. Jackson went over 300 passing yards with a 53-yard throw lofted to Chris Moore to the Indianapolis 19. Henry did the rest, capped by a 3-yard run for his third rushing touchdown, stretching Baltimore's lead to 38-16 early in the fourth. With under five minutes left in the first half, Laiatu Latu's sack and forced fumble to set the Colts up at the Ravens' 15. Taylor ran in untouched from 3 yards out to whittle the deficit to 28-13. Flowers left the Colts in the dust on a 54-yard touchdown in the second quarter. It was his fourth catch for 138 yards with more than six minutes left in the second quarter. Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey ripped the ball away from Taylor. Henry's second TD of the game, a 32-yard romp off left tackle, made it a 28-6 game. Ravens first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's debut was a smashing success. Baltimore scored two touchdowns on its first nine plays (10 including a penalty) and led 14-6 only 11 minutes into the game. Roquan Smith intercepted Jones to give the Ravens only 31 yards to paydirt, which Baltimore covered in six plays. Henry cut back a stretch running play designed to go right and shuffled into the end zone untouched from 4 yards out for a 14-6 lead. Henry's 123rd career touchdown pulled him even with Marcus Allen for third on the all-time list, then he passed Allen on his second score in the second quarter. He added TD No. 3 in the first minute of the fourth quarter. Only LaDainian Tomlinson (145) and leader Emmitt Smith (164) have more career rushing touchdowns in NFL history. Baltimore's first play from scrimmage was Jackson's 49-yard pass to Flowers to the Indianapolis 2. Jackson sprinted to the left pylon for a touchdown on a designed run two plays later, responding to the Colts' opening-drive touchdown run by Taylor. Ravens cornerback T.J. Tampa was ruled out in the first quarter with a knee injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vintage Josh Allen game lifts Bills over Texans in back-and-forth affair
item.description: Josh Allen accounted for four touchdowns and tossed the decisive 34-yard scoring pass to Joshua Palmer with 1:36 remaining as the Buffalo Bills won in Houston for the first time in 20 years with a wild 36-31 victory over the Texans in the season opener for both teams on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Josh Allen accounted for four touchdowns and tossed the decisive 34-yard scoring pass to Joshua Palmer with 1:36 remaining as the Buffalo Bills won in Houston for the first time in 20 years with a wild 36-31 victory over the Texans in the season opener for both teams on Sunday afternoon. Allen completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns and added two rushing scores while winning in Houston for the first time in five career attempts, including the postseason. The touchdown throw to Palmer capped a seven-play, 96-yard drive. Houston had one last chance at overcoming the deficit and reached the Buffalo 9-yard line. But on third-and-goal from the 18, Greg Rousseau sacked Houston's CJ Stroud and forced a fumble that teammate Terrel Bernard recovered at the Bills' 24 with nine seconds left to seal it. Dalton Kincaid had five receptions for 130 yards and DJ Moore had five catches for 100 yards and one touchdown in his Buffalo debut. Tyler Bass kicked three field goals and Rousseau had two sacks as the Bills won in Joe Brady's first game as head coach. David Montgomery rushed for two touchdowns and caught another in his Texans debut, while Stroud completed 26 of 38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns, including one to Nico Collins. Buffalo's winning excursion began at its own 4-yard line with 3:13 remaining. Allen's 35-yard pass to Kincaid moved the ball to the Houston 33 with 1:53 left. Three plays later, Allen connected with Palmer on a deep post with 1:36 remaining. A two-point pass failed. The Bills snapped a six-game losing streak in Houston. Buffalo hadn't won there since 2006 when J.P. Losman was the quarterback. Houston took a 28-27 lead when Stroud connected with Montgomery on a 7-yard scoring pass with 13:34 remaining in the game. The Bills regained the lead on Bass' 33-yard field goal with 10:31 left, but the Texans countered with Ka'imi Fairbairn's 58-yard field goal with 6:44 remaining. Allen rushed for two scores and passed for one as the Bills built a 24-21 halftime lead. After Bass opened the scoring with a 46-yard field goal midway through the first quarter, Montgomery scored from the 1 with 32 seconds left in the period. Allen avoided the rush and scampered 21 yards for a touchdown to give the Bills a 10-7 lead with 12:46 remaining in the second quarter. This time, Montgomery raced 18 yards to put Houston back ahead with 4:48 left. Allen scored from the 1 to give Buffalo a 17-14 lead with 3:59 remaining. After forcing a punt, the Bills went 96 yards on three plays as Allen hit Kincaid for 38 yards and Moore for 15 before tossing a 43-yard touchdown pass to Moore for a 10-point advantage with 1:29 left. The Texans responded with Stroud's 12-yard scoring strike to Collins with 26 seconds remaining. Buffalo increased its lead to 27-21 on Bass' 34-yard field goal with 4:24 left in the third quarter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cam Schlittler dominant as Yankees shut out Mets
item.description: Cam Schlittler pitched six innings of one-hit ball in his latest stellar outing, and the host New York Yankees earned a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets in the final game of the Subway Series on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cam Schlittler pitched six innings of one-hit ball in his latest stellar outing, and the host New York Yankees earned a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets in the final game of the Subway Series on Sunday afternoon. Ben Rice and Austin Wells provided the only runs of the game via solo home runs as the Yankees (86-63) won for the 18th time in 26 games and lowered their magic number for clinching a postseason spot to one. Schlittler (14-6) allowed only Brett Baty's double with two outs in the fifth. It was the third time in his 45 career starts that Schlittler allowed one hit and the second time this season. The right-hander struck out eight and walked two. He moved past Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski (1.952 ERA) for the major league lead by lowering his ERA to 1.949. Schlittler threw 60 of 94 pitches for strikes and ended his outing after taking Bo Bichette's comebacker off the back of his right leg. The ball deflected to catcher Wells, who threw to Luis Garcia Jr. at first base to complete the out. Afterward, Schlittler headed straight to the clubhouse but seemed fine. Rice slugged his third career leadoff home run and Wells homered in the third off Mets starter Christian Scott (4-5). Scott allowed two runs on three hits in six innings. The right-hander struck out Aaron Judge three times and finished with seven strikeouts to go with two walks. Judge went 0-for-3 and is 3-for-17 since being activated from the injured list. The Yankees' Brent Headrick tossed a 1-2-3 seventh and Paul Blackburn got Lindor on a pop-up to end the eighth. David Bednar stranded a runner and notched his 34th save in 37 chances. The Mets (69-80) were blanked for the 14th time as Lindor and Juan Soto were a combined 0-for-7 with four strikeouts. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reports: Jets WR Omar Cooper Jr. sustained high ankle sprain
item.description: New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is believed to have sustained a high ankle sprain in the team's season-opening 23-10 win Sunday at the Tennessee Titans, according to multiple media reports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is believed to have sustained a high ankle sprain in the team's season-opening 23-10 win Sunday at the Tennessee Titans, according to multiple media reports. Per NFL Network, Cooper had X-rays, which were negative. Meanwhile, veteran safety Minkah Fitzpatrick sustained a strained left groin after he was on the field for just six plays in his Jets debut. New York coach Aaron Glenn didn't provide much of an update on either player's status, except to say that he's "not too worried about them at all." Cooper, selected in the first round (30th overall) in April's draft out of Indiana, caught his lone target for a 30-yard gain to set up a touchdown on the Jets' opening drive. Fitzpatrick is a five-time Pro Bowler and three-time first-team All-Pro beginning his first season with his third NFL team. He had 690 tackles, 21 interceptions, 60 pass breakups, six forced fumbles and seven recoveries in eight seasons for the Miami Dolphins (2018-19, 2025) and Pittsburgh Steelers (2019-24). --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets dominate Titans to ruin Robert Saleh's Tennessee debut
item.description: Kenyon Sadiq and Breece Hall ran for touchdowns, Geno Smith threw for 215 yards and the visiting New York Jets put the clamps on the Tennessee Titans to start the season with a 23-10 win on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kenyon Sadiq and Breece Hall ran for touchdowns, Geno Smith threw for 215 yards and the visiting New York Jets put the clamps on the Tennessee Titans to start the season with a 23-10 win on Sunday afternoon. Smith was 19 of 24 in winning his first start for the Jets (1-0) since 2016. Hall added 102 yards on 22 rushes as the Jets outgained Tennessee 367-195 and hogged the ball for 38 minutes and 46 seconds. Cam Ward struggled most of the game for the Titans (0-1), hitting 19 of 32 passes for only 140 yards and a late touchdown. Ward played under constant pressure as New York recorded three sacks and forced him into inaccurate throws. The outcome spoiled the first game for Robert Saleh as Tennessee's coach. The ex-Jets boss and his coaching staff got a glimpse of how much ground the team has to cover to be competitive in the AFC South, let alone against the league's top teams. The Jets wasted little time putting their stamp on the game, taking the opening kickoff and marching 60 yards in eight plays. Sadiq covered the last 3 yards on a tight end reverse, rumbling inside the left front pylon of the end zone at the 10:45 mark. Joey Slye connected on a 42-yard field goal with 5:03 left in the first quarter for the Titans. But Tennessee wouldn't score again until Ward found Elic Ayomanor for an 11-yard touchdown strike with 2:42 remaining in the game. Jason Sanders drilled a 33-yard field goal with 5:03 remaining in the second quarter to make it 10-3 New York. It capped a 19-play drive, 15 of them runs, that lasted a whopping 11:48. Hall upped the advantage to 17-3 with 9:41 left in the third quarter on a 4-yard run that finished an 80-yard drive. Smith fueled it with completions of 31 and 40 yards to Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, respectively. Sanders added a 51-yard field goal with 4:33 remaining in the period and a 52-yarder with five minutes left in the game --Field Level Media

item.title: Memorial statue of conservative activist Charlie Kirk vandalized
item.description: A newly installed memorial statue of slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk was vandalized overnight in Phoenix on Sunday, according to the organization that he founded.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Ax
item.content:encoded: A newly installed memorial statue of slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk was vandalized overnight in Phoenix on Sunday, according to the organization that he founded. The statue was defaced with red paint, according to a post on X from Tyler Bowyer, chief operating officer of Turning Point Action, the youth-focused political organization founded by Kirk. Phoenix police confirmed they had responded to calls on Sunday morning regarding a vandalized memorial outside the headquarters of Turning Point and asked anyone with information to call. "This morning we woke up to radical criminals vandalizing our headquarters," Bowyer posted on X, along with photos of the statue and a separate sign that also had been spray-painted. The statue was unveiled on Thursday to mark one year since Kirk was fatally shot during a Turning Point event in Utah on September 10, 2025. The man accused of killing Kirk, Tyler Robinson, has [USN:L6N44S0ZO TEXT:"pleaded not guilty"] to murder charges and could face the death penalty if convicted. Kirk's activism and legacy divided many in the country. Civil rights advocates criticized Kirk for rhetoric they called racist, anti-immigrant, transphobic, and misogynist, citing his public remarks denigrating Black Americans, LGBTQ+ communities, Muslims and immigrants. His supporters described him as a defender of conservative values and public debate who galvanized young voters for President Donald Trump in the 2024 election.

item.title: VAR in focus as Haaland goal gives Man City controversial derby win
item.description: Erling Haaland's controversial goal proved to be the winner for Manchester City at Old Trafford.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Erling Haaland's controversial goal proved to be the winner for Manchester City against Manchester United in their Premier League clash at Old Trafford on Sunday, but it is unlikely the big Norwegian will have the last word as debate rages whether the derby goal should have been allowed to stand. Video reviews showed Haaland was onside when the ball was played, but an attempt by City midfielder Enzo Fernandez to head it into the net was seemingly ignored in the VAR deliberations, with the Argentinian appearing to be in an offside position when Josko Gvardiol played the initial ball in. The Premier League Match Centre said on social media platform X that Fernandez didn't play the ball, and therefore the goal was allowed to stand, but needless to say the red side of Manchester did not agree with that assessment. "I just don't get it, I really don't get it, I can't understand how we're trying to help referees, putting so many layers behind them, so many people, bodies and screens, and they can't make the right decision," United coach Michael Carrick fumed. "It's worrying if that's how the game's seen by those who are officiating it ... I can't be too critical of the players, and I won't be because I think we've done a lot of good things. Today we didn't quite find what we needed. The United boss, who has taken four points from his first four league games of the season, couldn't hide his disappointment. "I'm feeling for the fans today. We haven't got as many points as we would've liked at this stage, there's no getting away from that. We've just got to move on and get winning again." Defender Lisandro Martinez was equally frustrated. "I think it was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He was there. I went to him because he was there in front of me, that's why Haaland was free at the back," he explained. "I want to be calm now, I want to control myself, it's so hard, because you lose, you lose a derby, you lose three points at home ... it's unacceptable. Because it's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice."
